name: Honey never goes bad

hook_variants.template: A food that never expires. Found edible after 3,000 years.
What food was still edible after 3,000 years in a tomb?
Forget canned food. This one has a shelf life of forever.

sections.text: Honey almost never spoils. Archaeologists ate 3,000-year-old honey from Egyptian tombs.
Two reasons: it's mostly sugar, and it has almost no water. Microbes can't survive in it.
sections.title: the secret

sections.text: Bees make it 17 to 18 percent water, then air out the hive to dry it further.
sections.subtitle: water content — too low for bacteria

sections.text: It even has a built-in antibacterial, hydrogen peroxide, produced by an enzyme bees add.
sections.title: defense system

sections.text: The only catch: moisture gets in, it can ferment. Keep it sealed and it outlives you.
Follow for more facts that sound too good to be true.

facts.claim: Archaeologists found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still edible
Honey is stable because its low water content and high sugar content prevent microbial growth
Bees produce honey with ~17-18% water content

titles: Honey doesn't go bad. Here's why.
